name: Can I renovate an older house myself to save money?

mainEntity.name: Can I renovate an older house myself to save money?

acceptedAnswer.text: Do-it-yourself work may suit limited cosmetic tasks, but demolition and system changes in an older home can expose hazards and create coordination problems. Context: permit rules, lead-paint risk, concealed damage, structural work, and plumbing or electrical changes make professional planning more valuable. Key factors: task complexity, tools, documentation, occupied conditions, and whether the work affects permitted construction. Practical guidance: reserve DIY for clearly defined work that does not compromise the coordinated scope, and disclose it before design begins. Do not remove painted surfaces or open walls casually in a pre-1978 home. Professional coordination is especially useful when several trades or rooms connect.
acceptedAnswer.description: DIY may work for limited cosmetic tasks, but demolition, structural changes, plumbing, electrical work, and painted-surface disturbance can create safety, permit, and coordination problems. Define DIY boundaries before construction so the professional scope remains accurate.
